concepts.gloss: The Goat Who Would Not Come In
concepts.hook: A nanny goat refused the byre in the hungry winter and stayed out on the cliff, so Hesk keeps her at the north edge where every hearth-door can still see her.

concepts.gloss: The Ewe of the First Blanket
concepts.hook: Her fleece was spun into the first hearth-blanket, and her stars lie scattered like tufts caught on a fence-wire.
A dog tied to the Reel's post lifts its head at every footstep on the path, though the one it waits for has not come up the cliff in forty years.

concepts.gloss: The Cat on the Drying Net
concepts.hook: She sleeps on the net to keep mice out of the grain-jar, and her stars shift each time the net is hung or taken down.
She carried salt up the cliff path for forty winters, and her stars are the marks left by the load on her back.

concepts.gloss: The Hen Who Sat Nine Clutches
concepts.hook: She brooded eggs out of season until the shell-count went wrong, and the elders still use her stars to check the household tally.
She plucked the down from her own breast to line a child's cradle, and Hesk keeps her stars on the pole where the warm feathers are counted.

concepts.gloss: The Old Gannet of the Stacks
concepts.hook: She has nested on the same sea-stack longer than any house has stood, and the elders say she counts the stacks each dawn so none goes missing.

concepts.gloss: The Crow Who Stole the Tally-String
concepts.hook: A crow took a knotted count-string from the Reel's table, and though the string was spent long ago, the crow still flies the knots in its beak.
Each spring the shearwater finds its burrow by a star-track that the Spindle lays down, and fishers steer by it when they want their own children home.
A wren that roosts in the elders' roof-thatch has stars that are only the holes where the light comes through, and the household says a wren in the roof means no one will die that winter.

concepts.gloss: The Puffin Who Lost Her Burrow
concepts.hook: A puffin blown off course in a storm could not find her way back to her burrow, so she hangs in the north, still asking the way.
A limpet clings to the flat stone under the family hearth and has not moved in living memory, which is why the Ilvari say to be as hard to shift as a limpet.
An eel lives in the household well and is fed by the eldest each evening, and its coils are the loops the Reel winds when a house has kept its water clean.
Children count the mussels on the low bed each year at the turn of the tide, and the stars are the shells they have counted and never finished.

concepts.gloss: The Hermit Crab with a House
concepts.hook: A crab that wears a dead house-shell for a home drags it across the stars, and the Spindle keeps it as a reminder that a home can be carried.

concepts.gloss: The Seal Wife at the Hearth
concepts.hook: A seal wife whose skin was burnt came to live beside a hearth and kept the house for a hundred winters, and her stars sit closest to the Reel.

concepts.gloss: The Old Cod of the Deep Shelf
concepts.hook: The elders fish the great cod of the deep shelf and count its years by the rings in its scales, and its stars are the marks of the oldest year still living.
A creature that unpicks knots and eats the loose ends is why children are taught to tie every hitch twice, and its stars are the tangles it left behind.
A household spirit under the boards knocks when the house is kept right and goes quiet when the fire is let go out, and her stars are the knocks counted in the dark.
A salt-wight climbs the cliff wall at night and must be given bread at the top or it will pull the house-rope loose, so its stars hang over the door-hole.
A bone-thin thing weaves at night and undoes whatever the day has finished, so the weavers leave the last thread loose for it and its stars are the threads it has taken.
A kelp root clings to the rock beneath the house and keeps the whole family from being swept off the cliff, and the Ilvari name it for the anchor that holds a home.

concepts.gloss: The Sheaf Left for the Dead
concepts.hook: A barley sheaf is left standing at the cairn for the dead to eat from, and its ears are the stars the Reel counts in the autumn.
Nettles are cut each spring at the edge of the field for the cloth of the house, and the stars are the stalks left standing to seed for next year.
A rowan tree grows by the door of every house and keeps the wind-wights out, and its red berries are the stars that stay lit through the longest night.
Frost comes to the door each winter asking to be let in, and the household that gives it a cup of warm water is left alone, so the Spindle keeps its stars in a ring like a cup set out.

concepts.gloss: The Hearth-Smoke That Climbs and Stops
concepts.hook: The smoke from a house rises straight into the Spindle and then stops at a height no one has reached, and the elders say it is waiting for someone to come home.
A snow-spirit falls on the cliffs each winter and counts every flake against the household's stores, and its stars are the flakes it has tallied for the Reel.

concepts.gloss: The Dead Calm on the Water
concepts.hook: A still-air wind sits on the sea for days before a storm and does not stir, and fishers look for it in the Spindle before they risk the boats.
